result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as mock resources, whatever the rest of the name is. That covers plain `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/`, `mock-größe/` and `mock模拟/`. I didn't write new tests for these cases or run the patterns against example paths.

The change is in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (around line 393). I replaced the character class `[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+` in the two path patterns with `[^/]*`:
- `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*`
- `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`

- **Within one folder name:** the match can't run past a `/`, and the pattern still needs a `/` right before `mock`. So `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` stay outside the rule.
- **Old test folders:** `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` all still match, because the new pattern accepts everything the old one did.
- **Backslash paths:** `SourceFileFilter.matches` already tries each path with backslashes converted to `/`, so Windows-style paths work without further changes.

The scoping and convention tests in the `codeanalyzer` module ran with no failures.
